correctness.rationale: For all n≥2, adjacent-value transposition exactly pairs the two conditional inverse-descent measures. It leaves every record indicator unchanged except a possible 1→0 at the second high-value occurrence. The exceptional event has conditional probability 2/[m(m−1)], and independent hypergeometric order-statistic positions yield the displayed triangular matrix; simplification, diagonal, and telescoping are exact. The standalone script exhaustively checked all 168 entries and every coupling pair for n=2,…,8 as corroboration, not proof.

originality.rationale: The new explicit record-position by inverse-descent value-rank covariance matrix and simultaneous conditional monotone coupling are not stated in the inspected sources. The strongest comparator, Baril–Vajnovszki’s set-valued bijection, encodes relevant joint data and leaves a material implicit-priority risk. Jin’s broad generating functions do cover count-level quantities; this is acknowledged, and the global covariance is not presented as original. Earlier record–position-descent dependence is a different statistic.
residual_risks: The exact kernel could be recoverable as an unstated consequence of the 2016 set-valued coding, and a more specialized historical result could have been missed.

value.rationale: A structural conditional stochastic dominance theorem for the entire record-vector, an exact full-rank triangular rankwise covariance kernel with sharp zero set, and a quantitatively boundary-concentrated aggregate dependence directly characterize how local value-rank disorder influences online records. This natural duality distinguishes inverse descents from previously studied position descents and applies to every size, without arbitrary slices.
